title: Adjectives after nouns, un / una, words for car, grande, rojo, en

cards.title: Describing words go after the noun
cards.body: Adjectives (words you can put 'is' in front of: big, yellow) normally come after the noun in Spanish. There's some flexibility for emphasis.

examples.en: I want to buy a digital camera.
I want to buy it (the camera).

cards.title: Words for 'car'
cards.body: It varies by region, but most people understand all of them: coche, carro, auto, máquina. Un = a (masculine). Gender belongs to the word, so the same object can be masculine or feminine.

examples.es: un coche / un carro / un auto

cards.title: grande; plurals agree
cards.body: Grande = big (think 'grand'). In the plural, the, the noun and the adjective all become plural.

examples.es: el auto grande / la máquina grande

cards.title: 'Do you see?' vs 'Can you see?'
cards.body: Spanish more often says '¿ves…?' (do you see). 'Can you…' with puedes plus a 'to' form is a handy thinking shortcut while you're building fluency.

examples.en: Do you see the big car?
Can you see the big car?

cards.title: Shortcut verbs: puedo, debo, quiero…
cards.body: Using these with a 'to' form is easier to build, even if natives might say it differently: 'I don't find it'. You'll notice and adapt over time.

cards.title: Start with the verb
cards.body: The verb is the backbone: first work out who's doing it (quedo), then add the little word (me quedo).

cards.title: rojo = red; en = in
cards.body: J is the throaty sound; the initial r is rolled.

examples.en: I'm staying in the red car.
examples.es: Me quedo en el auto rojo.

examples.en: I've bought myself a red car.
examples.es: Me he comprado un auto rojo.

practice.en: I want to buy a digital camera.
I want to buy it (the camera).
Do you (informal) see the big car?
I'm staying in the red car.
es: Me quedo en el auto rojo
Me quedo en el coche rojo
Me quedo en el carro rojo
practice.why: en = in; rojo after the noun.

practice.en: I've bought myself a red car.
es: Me he comprado un auto rojo
Me he comprado un coche rojo
Me he comprado un carro rojo
practice.why: me he comprado + un auto rojo.
